Pause every rep on the chest and keep your shoulder blades pinned. Rest 3 minutes on bench sets.
Every 4th week, halve the bench sets. Shoulder pain means drop the volume, not push through.

name: Somax Powerlifter GPP & Conditioning
description: A 30-minute general fitness session for strength athletes: sled work, carries and easy bike intervals to boost recovery and work capacity without hurting your lifting.
whoItsFor: Intermediate powerlifters and strength trainees who get puffed between sets or want better recovery between heavy days.
howToRun: Once or twice a week on non-lifting days, or after an upper-body session. Keep it at 6-7/10 effort.
No muscle soreness allowed: sled and carries have almost no lowering, so they don't eat into recovery.
Progress by adding a sled trip or a minute of bike each week. If tomorrow's lifting suffers, cut it back.
No sled? Do loaded farmer walks and incline walking instead.

name: Somax First Pull-up Builder
description: Dead hangs, scapular pulls, band-assisted pull-ups and slow negatives: a step-by-step path to your first strict pull-up.
whoItsFor: Anyone who can't yet do a pull-up (or can do only one) and has a bar at home, at the gym or in the park.
howToRun: Three times a week on non-consecutive days. Add it to the end of another workout or do it on its own.
Build the dead hang to 30-60 seconds, then add scapular pulls. Negatives: jump to the top and take 5 seconds to lower.
Each week, use a lighter band or add a negative. Test a strict pull-up every 2 weeks; most people get one in 6-12 weeks.
Once you can do 3 strict reps, move on to the BWF Recommended Routine or Somax Park Calisthenics – Intermediate.

name: Somax Push-up Builder
description: Incline push-ups, eccentrics and practice sets to go from zero (or a few) to 20 strict push-ups.
whoItsFor: Beginners who can't do many full push-ups yet and want a 15-minute routine at home, three times a week.
howToRun: Three times a week. Find your level: wall, kitchen bench, low table or floor. Use the lowest height you can do 8 good reps from.
Practice sets: do about 60-70% of your max per set, stopping 1-2 reps short of failure.
When you hit 4 x 12 at one height, go lower. Test your max floor push-ups every 2 weeks.
Keep a straight line from head to heels and elbows at about 45 degrees from your body.

name: Somax Park Calisthenics – Beginner
description: A full-body workout using an outdoor fitness station or playground: bar hangs and rows, bench push-ups, step-ups and lunges.
whoItsFor: Beginners who'd rather train outdoors for free. Most local parks and beaches in Australia have a bar and a bench.
howToRun: Three days a week. Bring water and a towel, and check the equipment is dry and solid.
Do the exercises as a circuit (one set of each in a row), rest 90 seconds, and repeat 3 times.
Progress row and push-up angles: lower the body (or the bar) a little each week. Add reps before making it harder.
Sun-smart: train early or late in summer, and wear sunscreen and a hat.

name: Somax Park Calisthenics – Intermediate
description: Pull-ups, dips, archer push-ups, Bulgarian split squats and hanging core work at the outdoor gym.
whoItsFor: Intermediate exercisers who can do at least 5 pull-ups and 10 dips and want to keep progressing outdoors.
howToRun: Three days a week, or four alternating with running. Rest 90-120 seconds between sets of the main moves.
Stop 1-2 reps short of failure. When you hit 3 x 12 of a move, use a harder version (e.g. slower pull-ups, archer push-ups).
Short of a dip station? Use parallel bars or a bench (bench dips) and add a pause.
Track your reps. Plateaued for 3 weeks? Take an easy week, then switch to harder versions with fewer reps.

name: Somax Calisthenics PPL – Push
description: Dips, pike push-ups, pseudo-planche push-ups and diamond push-ups.
whoItsFor: Intermediate bodyweight trainees (5+ pull-ups, 15+ push-ups) who want a structured split for more muscle and strength, at home or in the park.
howToRun: Push, Pull, Legs, rest, repeat (6 days on, 1 off) or once each per week plus skill practice on other days.
Pick the hardest version you can do for the target reps with 1-2 in reserve. Move up a step when you hit the top of the range on all sets.
Legs are the weak spot of most calisthenics plans: don't skip them, and add a backpack load when they get easy.
Every 5th week, halve the sets. Wrists and elbows sore? Do fewer high-rep sets and more slow, controlled reps.

name: Somax Pistol Squat Progression
description: Box pistols, assisted pistols, cossack squats and ankle mobility on the way to a full single-leg squat.
whoItsFor: Bodyweight trainees with decent squats who want real leg strength without weights, and the balance and mobility that come with it.
howToRun: Twice a week, after your main workout or on its own.
Start with box pistols to a height you control on the way down. Lower the box a few centimetres each week.
Holding a pole or doorframe for balance is fine early on. A light weight held in front can help you stay balanced.
Knee pain means a higher box or slower lowering. Tight ankles? Raise your heel on a small plate.

name: Somax Handstand & L-sit Skills
description: Practice time for two classic skills: wall handstands and L-sits, with wrist prep and compression drills.
whoItsFor: Intermediate trainees who can hold a 60-second plank and do 10 push-ups and want their first freestanding handstand and L-sit.
howToRun: Three short sessions a week, before strength work while you're fresh. Treat it as practice: quality holds, never to failure.
Chest-to-wall handstand: build to 60 seconds total, then add kick-ups and toe pulls off the wall.
L-sit: progress foot-supported, then one leg, tuck, one leg straight, then full L. Build to 3 x 15-20 seconds per stage.
Wrists take time: always do the wrist prep, and ease off if they ache for more than a day.

name: Somax Gymnastic Rings Foundations
description: Ring support holds, ring rows, ring push-ups, ring dips and false-grip hangs: the base for muscle-ups and stronger shoulders.
whoItsFor: Intermediate trainees who own a set of rings (hung from a bar, beam or tree) and want to build stability and pulling and pushing strength.
howToRun: Three times a week. Hang the rings so you can stand under them for rows and reach them from the ground for dips.
Support hold first: 3 x 30 seconds, rings turned out, before you try ring dips.
Make it harder by changing your body angle (rows, push-ups) or the ring height, then by adding reps.
Rings are unstable: go slowly, keep reps clean and stop when your shoulders shake past control.

name: Somax Weighted Calisthenics – A
description: Heavy weighted pull-ups and dips, then archer pull-ups and hanging leg raises.
whoItsFor: Advanced calisthenics trainees (12+ pull-ups, 20+ dips) who want maximal upper-body strength using a dip belt or weighted vest.
howToRun: Alternate A and B 3-4 times a week. Rest 2-3 minutes on weighted sets and 90 seconds on the rest.
Weighted lifts: a top set of 3-5 at RPE 8, then 2-3 back-off sets at 90%. Add 1.25-2.5kg when the top set moves well.
Keep strict form: full lockout on dips, chin over the bar and a dead hang at the bottom of pull-ups.
Deload every 5th week (bodyweight only, half the sets). Elbow pain? Reduce weighted volume first.

name: Somax Calisthenics Ladder Conditioning
description: Pull-up, push-up and squat ladders against the clock: lots of quality reps, a big calorie burn and better work capacity.
whoItsFor: Intermediate exercisers who can do a few pull-ups and want a tough 30-minute fat-loss session with just a bar.
howToRun: Up to three times a week, not on back-to-back days. Keep 1-2 reps in reserve on every rung so form holds up.
Ladder: 1 pull-up, 2 push-ups, 3 squats; then 2-4-6; keep climbing to 5-10-15, then start again at 1 until the 20 minutes are up.
Track total rounds and try to beat it next time. Swap in inverted rows if pull-ups run out.
Fat loss comes mostly from your eating; this session builds fitness and holds muscle.
